query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tuning the composition of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be used to modify their magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
generation.mechanism: Changes in magnetic exchange interactions and spin fluctuations
generation.predicted_outcome: Modification of magnetic transition temperatures and magnetocaloric effect
generation.boundary: Limits of solubility and phase stability
generation.uncertainty: Specific effects of composition tuning on magnetic and magnetocaloric properties are uncertain without further experimentation

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of elemental ratios in non-equiatomic HEAs, followed by characterization of magnetic and magnetocaloric properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no correlation is found between composition tuning and changes in magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, the hypothesis is falsified
